documents.title: Interim Policy Prohibiting Entering Confidential Information into Generative AI
documents.summary: A short interim IT data-protection policy applying to all WPI students, faculty and staff. It bans entering confidential institutional, employee or student data into generative AI tools, points to a list of authorized tools, and says a fuller policy is being developed. It says nothing about coursework use of AI.
documents.stance_why: The document says 'Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools' and points to 'authorized tools'. It bans one category of input, not AI use in general, and sets no coursework rule or delegation, so restrict.
documents.resolution_why: Coder A chose restrict, B chose prohibit. The ban covers only confidential data entry, and the document keeps other generative AI use open (authorized tools list). The codebook defines prohibit as AI use banned for the governed work and restrict as a narrow limit, so restrict.

units.why: Warns that information entered into a generative AI tool 'immediately becomes part of the generative AI's information database', a fact explaining why the rule exists. P50 covers that tools retain prompts; informs, not a command.
units.anchor: immediately becomes part of the generative AI’s information database
units.frag_start: Members of the WPI community may

units.why: States that 'any private or confidential information entered into a generative AI tool is at risk of becoming public', the risk consequence behind the data rule. Rationale for P50; informs.
units.anchor: confidential information entered into a generative AI tool is at risk of becoming public

units.why: The policy is put in place 'on an interim basis' while 'a more comprehensive policy is collaboratively developed', so it is provisional and will be replaced: P54. It describes the policy itself, so the actor is admin.
units.anchor: put in place on an interim basis
units.policy: The policy is in place on an interim basis to deal with immediate risks of unintended disclosure of Confidential Information while a more comprehensive policy is collaboratively developed.
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on type, phase and modality. Actor differed: A said admin, B said all. The passage describes the status of the policy and what the institution is doing ('being put in place', 'collaboratively developed'), not a duty on community members, so admin. Policy wording follows the source sentence.

units.why: States the intent to 'integrate language related to generative AI usage' into the revised Data Classification and Usage Policy: a planned revision of an existing policy to include AI. P54 fits; the review process itself is the separate P84 unit.
units.anchor: We intend to integrate language related to generative AI usage into that revised policy.
units.resolution_why: Found only by B (P54, intent to integrate AI language). A folded this sentence into one P84 unit about the review. The source has two distinct statements: the review of the 2019 policy (process) and the intent to add AI language (planned revision). Kept as its own unit, P54, anchor-only.

units.why: Says WPI has been 'collaboratively reviewing WPI's Data Classification and Usage Policy', last revised in 2019: how the guidance is being developed, so P84. The planned AI language is the separate P54 unit.
units.anchor: we have been collaboratively reviewing WPI’s Data Classification and Usage Policy
units.policy: WPI is collaboratively reviewing its Data Classification and Usage Policy, last revised in 2019.
units.resolution_why: Type, actor and modality agreed (P84, admin, informs). Phase differed: A over-time, B general. The passage describes an ongoing review of an existing policy, which is review and revision, so over-time. A's policy also included the intent to add AI language; that is now the separate P54 unit, so the wording is cut to the review.

units.why: 'This Policy applies to all students, faculty, and staff at WPI' sets who the policy binds. Scope statement, P61, the nearest type.
units.anchor: This Policy applies to all students, faculty, and staff at WPI.
units.fit_note: Sets who the policy binds rather than defining AI.

units.why: Defines 'Confidential Information' (confidential institutional and employee data, and student data not publicly available; examples include SSNs, passwords, HIPAA and FERPA records) to set what may not be entered. Scope definition, P61.
units.anchor: confidential WPI institutional data, confidential WPI employee data, and WPI student data
units.policy: Confidential Information means confidential WPI institutional data, confidential WPI employee data, and WPI student data that is not publicly available and should not be released publicly, including but not limited to social security numbers, financial account information, passwords, driver's license numbers, HIPAA-protected health care information, human resources and personnel information, FERPA-protected student records, and gift and donor information.
units.fit_note: Defines the protected data category the AI ban covers, not AI or AI tools.
units.resolution_why: Both coders gave P61 for the definition. B also coded the bullet list (FERPA, HIPAA etc.) as a second unit. The bullets are the 'including but not limited to' part of the same definition sentence, so they are one rule, not two; B's second unit is dropped and its list is merged into this unit's policy. Frag_end extended to the end of the bullet list.

units.why: 'Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools' is a direct ban on one kind of input, binding everyone: must-not. P50 fits best; P20 and P49 concern assignment materials or course content, not confidential institutional data.
units.anchor: Do not enter Confidential Information into generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Google Gemini, etc.).
units.resolution_why: Type, actor, phase and modality agreed. unit_stance differed: A restrict, B prohibit. The rule bans only one category of input (confidential data) and leaves other use of generative AI tools open, with a list of authorized tools, so it is a narrow ban, which the codebook calls restrict, not a ban on AI use.

units.why: 'A list of authorized tools can be found on the ITS knowledgebase' points users to an institutionally authorized tool list: P92. It does not itself say only authorized tools may be used.
units.anchor: A list of authorized tools can be found on the ITS knowledgebase
units.policy: A list of authorized tools can be found on the ITS knowledgebase or by contacting the ITS Service Desk.
units.fit_note: Only points to the list; it does not say authorized tools must be used.

units.why: 'you should seek guidance from your manager, Department Head or WPI's Information Technology Services ... before entering information in a generative AI tool' tells unsure users to ask first: P10, limited to data entry.
units.anchor: you should seek guidance from your manager, Department Head or WPI’s Information Technology Services
units.policy: Anyone with questions or concerns should seek guidance from their manager, Department Head or Information Technology Services before entering information in a generative AI tool.
units.fit_note: Addressed to employees and students generally, about data entry, not coursework permissions.
units.resolution_why: Type, actor, modality agreed. Phase differed: A general, B during-work. 'During-work' means assignments and studying; this document is not about coursework, and the advice applies to anyone at any time they might enter data, so general.

units.why: Names the 'Policy Sponsor: Chief Information Officer; Chief Information Security Officer' and the responsible department, stating who owns the policy: P80.
units.anchor: Policy Sponsor: Chief Information Officer; Chief Information Security Officer
units.policy: The policy sponsors are the Chief Information Officer and Chief Information Security Officer; the responsible department is Information Technology.

units.why: The effective-date lines record 'Presidential Approval' on December 4, 2023 and later extensions of the interim period: how and when the policy was adopted and extended, P84. Dated history, not a promise of review.
units.policy: The first interim policy took effect on December 4, 2023 with Presidential Approval, and the interim period has since been extended with Presidential Approval, the latest extension running Mar. 27, 2026 to Sept. 26, 2026.

notes: Only one included document: an IT data-protection interim policy with no coursework guidance. School, computing and course layers not coded (none found or deferred). The effective-date line has an inconsistent extension date (Sept. 25, 2026 - Mar. 26, 2026) in the source; not coded as a separate policy. Fit notes from both coders were kept (merged in the P61, P92, P10 units). No uncovered notes or new types.
